cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Humerus
cards.label: a

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates distally with the ulna at the trochlea and with the radius at the capitulum.
cards.label: a

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Capitulum, trochlea, medial and lateral epicondyles, coronoid fossa, radial fossa and olecranon fossa.
cards.label: a

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Common flexor origin attaches to the medial epicondyle; common extensor origin attaches to the lateral epicondyle; brachialis and triceps attach proximally/distally around the humerus.
cards.label: a

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Capitulum lies lateral and trochlea medial; olecranon fossa is posterior.
cards.label: a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ulna
cards.label: b

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates with the humeral trochlea at the trochlear notch and with the radius at the proximal and distal radioulnar joints.
cards.label: b

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Olecranon, coronoid process, trochlear notch, radial notch and ulnar tuberosity.
cards.label: b

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Triceps inserts on olecranon; brachialis inserts on coronoid process/ulnar tuberosity; pronator teres and flexor muscles attach in the proximal forearm region.
cards.label: b

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Olecranon projects proximally/posteriorly; radial notch lies laterally.
cards.label: b

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Radius
cards.label: c

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Articulates proximally with capitulum of humerus and radial notch of ulna; distally with scaphoid/lunate and ulna.
cards.label: c

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Head, neck, radial tuberosity and interosseous border.
cards.label: c

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Biceps brachii inserts on radial tuberosity; supinator wraps around proximal radius; pronator teres inserts on lateral radius.
cards.label: c

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Radial head is proximal and disc-shaped; radial tuberosity lies medially.
cards.label: c

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Articular capsule

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Proximally attaches around the distal humeral articular margins; distally attaches to the ulna and blends with the annular ligament around the radius.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Encloses and stabilises the elbow joint while allowing flexion-extension and forearm rotation at the proximal radioulnar joint.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Reinforced medially and laterally by collateral ligaments; relatively lax anteriorly and posteriorly to permit movement.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Radial (lateral) collateral ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends from the lateral epicondyle of humerus and blends mainly with the annular ligament.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Provides lateral stability to the elbow and resists varus stress.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Part of the lateral collateral ligament complex, adjacent to the annular ligament of the radius.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Injury to the lateral collateral complex can contribute to posterolateral rotatory instability.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ulnar (medial) collateral ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends from the medial epicondyle of humerus to the coronoid process and olecranon of ulna.

cards.question: Parts
cards.answer: Anterior, posterior and transverse bands.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Provides medial stability and resists valgus stress at the elbow.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Can be injured by repetitive valgus loading, especially in throwing athletes.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Annular ligament of the radius

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Attaches to the anterior and posterior margins of the radial notch of the ulna and encircles the radial head.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Holds the radial head against the ulna while permitting pronation and supination.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms a fibro-osseous ring with the radial notch around the radial head.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: In young children, radial head subluxation from the annular ligament causes nursemaid's elbow.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tendon of biceps brachii

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Continuation of the biceps brachii muscle distally.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Inserts on the radial tuberosity; the bicipital aponeurosis blends with forearm fascia.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transmits biceps force for forearm supination and elbow flexion.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Passes anterior to the elbow joint into the cubital fossa before inserting on the radius.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Distal biceps rupture weakens supination more than elbow flexion.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Oblique cord

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends from the ulna just distal to the radial notch to the radius just distal to the radial tuberosity.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Helps bind the proximal radius and ulna and may limit excessive distal displacement of the radius.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Runs inferolaterally from ulna to radius, opposite in fibre direction to much of the interosseous membrane.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Interosseous membrane

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Broad fibrous sheet spanning the interosseous borders of radius and ulna.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Binds radius and ulna, transmits load from radius to ulna and provides muscle attachment.

cards.question: Fibre direction
cards.answer: Most fibres run inferomedially from radius to ulna.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Separates anterior and posterior compartments of the forearm and contains openings for interosseous vessels.
